s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic and laboratory evidence of myocardial injury, complicated by hypotension
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain with increasing intensity
ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on ECG
Elevation of high-sensitive troponin T level
Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery on emergency angiography
key_facts: The patient is an older woman
The patient has a history of diabetes
The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain
The intensity of pain increased over time
Initial vital signs showed a normal heart rate and blood pressure
Blood pressure later fell to 60/40 mm Hg
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
ECG showed subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
ECG showed downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
High-sensitive troponin T level was elevated at 0.309 ng/mL
Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
Computer tomography angiography revealed contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion

shortlist.label: ST-elevation myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery

shortlist.label: Cardiogenic shock
shortlist.why_kept: Blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg, indicating hypotension, and the patient had evidence of myocardial injury

shortlist.label: Cardiac tamponade
shortlist.why_kept: Computer tomography angiography revealed pericardial effusion, which could be causing hypotension

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitive troponin T level and ECG changes consistent with myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: Right ventricular infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, which could indicate right ventricular involvement

raw.rationale: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, ECG findings of ST-segment elevation in multiple leads, and an elevated high-sensitive troponin T level, which are all consistent with an ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Additionally, emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cardiogenic shock
rejected.why: While the patient's blood pressure did fall, the primary issue appears to be the myocardial infarction itself, rather than cardiogenic shock being the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of cardiac tamponade, such as equalization of diastolic pressures or a large pericardial effusion causing hemodynamic compromise.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes ST-elevation myocardial infarction, but ST-elevation myocardial infarction is a more specific and accurate diagnosis based on the ECG findings and other evidence.

rejected.label: Right ventricular infarction
rejected.why: While the patient did have ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, which could suggest right ventricular infarction, the overall clinical picture and ECG findings are more consistent with an ST-elevation myocardial infarction involving the left circumflex artery.
